problem: The preceding R12 ellipse fix still refused finite major and normal components whenever their Euclidean norms exceeded binary64. In a direct scratch probe, normal=(1.5e308,1.5e308,0), major=(1,-1,0) and normal=(0,0,1), major=(1.5e308,1.5e308,0) each produced zero vertices, although the tested partial-arc vertices are finite. A tolerance-based 2D classifier also labeled very slightly tilted huge geometry as 2D even though its WCS Z displacement was around 1e295.

authority.scope: ELLIPSE uses WCS major/center and a plane normal; POLYLINE flag 8 selects 3D. Autodesk's 2D vertex API locates OCS Z on the owning polyline, so individual vertex Z cannot be relied on to preserve arbitrary WCS elevation.

implementation: Ellipse-specific DXF geometry validation and R12 tessellation normalize vectors by their largest finite component before computing directions. The tessellator factors the major scale, normalized norm, ratio, minor direction and each sampled sine via frexp/ldexp, avoiding premature overflow/underflow when the final minor contribution is representable. It refuses a nonzero component lost during vector normalization, an entirely underflowed minor axis, any nonfinite sampled vertex, and preserves the output destination. Exact XY normal and axis with zero elevation retain the classic 2D route; tilted or elevated geometry uses 3D vertices. The shared generic CIRCLE extrusion check is unchanged. The existing ratio>1 axis-swap path retains its earlier preflight/refusal limits.

validation.baseline: A scratch direct probe compiled with the c01e244d pre-follow-up drw_entities.cpp and linked to the local library printed normal=0 and major=0 vertices for the two independently chosen overflowing-norm cases. With the changed code the identical probe printed normal=2 and major=2.
validation.coverage: Generated direct and ASCII/Binary R12 partial/full controls verify analytically evaluated endpoints for overflowing-norm normal and major vectors, tilted 3D WCS flag/Z readback with and without extrusion, exact-XY 2D preservation, modern AC1027 ELLIPSE field readback, subnormal 1e-308 ratio with finite nonzero Z, and a partial arc with an unrepresentable full minor axis but representable sampled points. A full arc with a nonrepresentable sampled point and mixed-scale components lost during normalization refuse atomically and retry after correction. Existing ratio>1 overflow refusal and CIRCLE-normal behavior are retained. No fixtures are committed.
validation.focusedResult: 7/7 passed after the final underflow and near-tilt changes with the configured -Werror build.

limits: This is generated arithmetic and local codec/readback evidence, not native CAD rendering or a broad LibreCAD compatibility claim. For example, center=(0,0,-5e307), major=(1.5e308,1.5e308,0), normal=(1,-1,0), ratio=1, parameters 1.2..1.3 has a finite final Z but an individually overflowing sampled minor contribution. A portable shared-exponent summation that also preserves deep cancellation and subnormals has not been qualified, so this profile is explicitly refused and retried in the test. Axis normalization for ratio>1 with an overflowing major norm remains refused. A component that vanishes when normalizing a mixed-scale vector is conservatively refused; other extreme rounding boundaries remain unqualified. The ellipse-specific validation change also admits tested extreme finite ELLIPSE values on modern DXF input/output; local same-library readback does not prove native interpretation or rendering.
